summary: Jacques Giès (1950–2021) worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history/archaeology. He studied at Paris-Sorbonne University and Beaux-Arts de Paris, and served as Chief Curator of Chinese Painting at the Musée Guimet (~1980–2008).

Jacques May (1927–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as editor-in-chief for the École française d'Extrême-Orient and Hōbōgirin (~1972–1981), and was a professor at the University of Lausanne (~1977–1992).

Jacques P. Leider (b. 1962) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1987–1998) and served as director at the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2001.

Jacques Scheuer (b. 1942) works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Université catholique de Louvain and under Madeleine Biardeau at Sorbonne Nouvelle University. His career includes posts at Facultés Loyola Paris and Université catholique de Louvain.
Jadunath Sarkar (1870–1958) was an Indian historian. He studied at Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta (~1887–1892), where he later held an academic post (~1926–1928).
Jae-seong Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1995), studying under Yasunori Ejima.

Jagdish Kashyap (1908–1976) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1927–1931) and the University of Kelaniya (~1931–1934), and served as Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1971).

Jake H. Davis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Marlboro College, the University of Hawaii, and CUNY Graduate Center, he has held posts at City College of New York, NYU, Barre Center, and Brown University.

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer (1881–1962) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the Basel Mission, Oxford, and Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. He held posts at the University of Marburg (~1925–1927) and the University of Tübingen (1927–1945).

James A. Benn specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge, SOAS under Timothy H. Barrett, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., he held posts at Lewis & Clark College, Arizona State University, and McMaster University.

James A. Matisoff (b. 1937) is a linguist who studied at Harvard University (~1954–1958) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1962–1967). He subsequently held a long-term academic post at UC Berkeley (~1970–2006).

James A. Santucci works in religious studies and Indology. He held positions at California State University (attested 1998) and California State University, Fullerton, where he served as Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion (attested 2007).

James Atkinson (1780–1852) was a scholar in Iranian/Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh and served as Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College in 1818.

James B. Apple is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed graduate and doctoral studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, working with supervisors including John D. Dunne and teachers such as Geshe Lhundub Sopa and Jan Nattier.

James Blumenthal (1967–2014) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and held posts at Oregon State University and Maitripa College.

James Burgess (1832–1916) was an archaeologist and Indologist. He succeeded Alexander Cunningham in 1885 and served multiple terms as head of the Archaeological Survey of India (1873, 1881, 1886), also founding *The Indian Antiquary* and *Epigraphia Indica*.

James Burnell Robinson (b. 1944) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1967–1975) under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, then joined the University of Northern Iowa (~1975).

James C. Dobbins specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Yale University (1984) and served as the Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College (attested 2015–2019).

James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland (1792–1844) worked in Indology. He studied at the East India Company College and under Thomas Roebuck at Fort William College, later serving as professor of law at Presidency University, Kolkata.
James Duerlinger works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1964–1968) under Sheldon Pollock and held an academic post at the University of Iowa.
